terms.comment: Most often plural; the singular parēns is a father or a mother (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a parent: a father or a mother
terms.comment: Of either parent; the old writers called even a mother parēns in the masculine (Festus, in Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: it is kindness that makes parents, not necessity

sources: Lewis & Short: parens
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 24.
Quotation from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-phaedrus), checked against the edition named there.
